subject: Onboarding economics & implementation orchestration for Nimbus (batching, caching, quant)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ava Spencer <ava@nimbusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding economics & initial implementation checklist for Nimbus

Hi Ava —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, I put together a concise implementation checklist focused on unit economics so we can get Nimbus to your latency/throughput targets while keeping cost predictable. Attached is a first-pass SOW and a short onboarding checklist (Redwood-Onboard-Checklist.xlsx).

High-level ask: can you confirm the expected traffic profile for the first 3 months (avg requests/sec, p95 tokens per request) and whether you plan to pin a model family or want Redwood to recommend a quant/profile? That will drive our batching and KV-cache recommendations.

Quick summary of what we propose to cover in the kickoff workshop (30–45m):
- Measurement: capture baseline token counts and real sessions to derive batching window
- Batching/cooling: target batch sizes and latency buds; opt-in for micro-batching on spikes
- KV/prefix caching: identify stable prefixes (search prompts, instructions) for prefix cache
- Quantization profile: recommend FP16/8-bit quant profiles per workload and perf/cost tradeoffs
- Routing policy: region and tier routing + fallback model variants for graceful degradation

If you can share the three metrics above and confirm procurement contact, we can lock a date.

Attachments: Nimbus_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (stub), Redwood-Onboard-Checklist.xlsx (stub)

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior CS Manager, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
From: Ava Spencer <ava@nimbusai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding economics & initial implementation checklist for Nimbus

Sean — thanks for the checklist. Quick answers below and one ask from procurement:

Traffic profile (estimate for M1–M3):
- Avg requests/sec: 12 rps
- p95 tokens/request: ~320 tokens
- Peak bursts: up to 90 rps for short campaign windows

We would like Redwood to recommend a quant/profile; we prefer lower cost while keeping p95 generative latency <= 350ms.

Procurement contact: procurement@nimbusai.com — they will need the SOW and an initial pricing estimate. Also, security sent over a SOC 2 questionnaire that we expect you to respond to.

Thanks — happy to join the kickoff once you propose times.

— Ava
Head of Platform, Nimbus AI

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ava Spencer <ava@nimbusai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding economics & initial implementation checklist for Nimbus — proposed mutual action plan

Ava / Nimbus team —

Thanks for the numbers — that helps. Based on the profile (12 rps average, 320 tokens p95, 90 rps burst) we recommend the following phased approach. I put this in a MUTUAL ACTION PLAN so we have clear owners and milestones going into the kickoff: 

Phase 0 — Pre-kickoff (this week)
- Redwood: finalize quant recommendation draft (FP16 + 4-bit quant candidate for non-critical models) and share perf vs cost matrix. (Owner: Sean)
- Nimbus: provide 7 days of sanitized session traces (anonymized) for batching analysis. (Owner: Ava)

Phase 1 — Kickoff workshop (45m)
- Topics: traffic measurement, target batch latency, caching keys, rollout strategy, procurement / SOW questions
- Deliverable: agreed batching window, target batch size envelope, KV cache candidate prefixes, routing policy draft
- Owners: Redwood engineering (Monica + Karthik) + Nimbus platform

Phase 2 — Pilot (2 weeks)
- Redwood: deploy recommended quant profile to trial pool; enable prefix caching for top N stable prompts; set canary routing to fallback variant at 5% traffic. (Owner: Karthik)
- Nimbus: validate latency at p95 and signal any content/regression issues with a short eval set. (Owner: Ava)

Phase 3 — Ramp & optimize (ongoing)
- Tune batching windows and KV cache TTLs based on observed session patterns; evaluate cost delta and revert if quality regressions arise. (Owners: Redwood + Nimbus)

Attachments: I attached a SOW draft and the onboarding checklist again for procurement. Also linking the HubSpot deal and the shared Drive doc with the traces request.

Proposed kickoff slots (30–45m):
- Tue Aug 24 10:00–10:45 PT
- Tue Aug 24 14:00–14:45 PT
- Wed Aug 25 09:00–09:45 PT

If any of those work, Monica will send a calendar invite and a short runbook for the meeting. We will also prepare a focused perf run (short, synthetic) so we can show expected batch behavior.

Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: Confirming kickoff + SOW next steps (Nimbus)

Hi Ava / Nimbus procurement —

Following Sean's plan, confirming Tue Aug 24 14:00–14:45 PT for the kickoff. Monica (implementation lead) and Karthik (runtime engineer) will run the workshop. Agenda will be brief (see runbook attached) and focused on the mutual action plan in Sean's note.

Action items for procurement / security:
- Procurement: please review the attached SOW (Nimbus_SOW_draft_v1.pdf) and confirm any changes; we can finalize commercial terms in parallel with the pilot. (Requested by: Wed Aug 26)
- Security: please send the SOC 2 questionnaire to security@redwood.com and we'll assign our compliance lead to respond.

Technical asks for the kickoff: please upload the 7-day sanitized traces to the shared Drive link by EOD Mon Aug 23 so our batching analysis can run pre-meeting. If you prefer, we can do a short synthetic perf run in the kickoff but having traces significantly shortens the iteration loop.

If those sound good I'll send an invite and the meeting runbook. Looking forward to kicking this off.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
